title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) measuring whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 (exact binomial formulation described in Methods); paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We present preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostic artifacts, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness in this setting requires generated configurations to satisfy deterministic invariants such as reachability, policy compliance, workflow ordering, and group-level safety (e.g., "at least one interface up" constraints). Prior prototype systems and benchmarks illustrate feasibility but leave open questions about how much deterministic verification and bounded repair change operational correctness when comparisons reuse the same initial sampled candidate. This paper addresses that gap with a preregistered, artifact-grounded paired experiment.

Research question and estimand. Preregistered study CAND-2026-001 asked: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? The primary estimand is the paired difference in per-task binary acceptance (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Because the experiment enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics the estimand isolates the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair on an identical initial candidate (a repair-only effect). This design does not measure effects due to independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, temperature tuning, or mult-sample selection.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis reporting baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200 with contingency counts (n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused failure diagnosis for the single repaired pair using archived validator traces. (5) Detailed reproducibility guidance and bounded limitations tied to archived artifacts and reconciliation records.
sections.related_work:
We conducted a fresh literature investigation and verified records covering intent→configuration systems, generate–validate–repair patterns, and agentic-AI safety discussions relevant to NetOps. Prior intent-to-configuration prototypes and task-bench evaluations demonstrate that LLMs can synthesize device configurations from operator intents and that verification is advocated as a necessary guardrail [1],[2],[3]. However, the supplied literature primarily reports prototypes or cross-domain demonstrations and does not provide preregistered paired experiments that deterministically reuse identical initial samples to isolate repair-only effects.

Generate→validate→repair as a pattern appears in adjacent domains (automated program repair, test-in-the-loop synthesis) where external validators materially influence correctness outcomes; these works motivate guarded pipelines for operational tasks but do not substitute for NetOps-specific verifier-backed empirical evidence [4],[5],[6]. Survey and safety literature on agentic AI and LLM deployment documents failure modes (hallucination/confabulation) and argues for verifier gates and provenance; that conceptual groundwork motivated our guarded design but does not provide artifact-backed NetOps verifier outcomes [7],[8].

Synthesis and gap. The verified records show active work on intent-driven generators and proposals for guardrails, but they leave an empirical gap: few artifact-backed studies quantify the marginal verifier/repair effect when the exact same initial generated candidate is reused across conditions. Our experiment directly addresses that gap under tightly controlled deterministic verifier semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design freeze. The study was preregistered as CAND-2026-001 and froze the sampling plan, estimand, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), and analysis procedures prior to any model calls. The preregistration specified N = 200 tasks, pairwise episodes (baseline and guarded), one initial generation per task reused by both conditions, and at most one automated repair invocation per task. The preregistered primary test was an exact two-sided McNemar implemented via the exact binomial tail: for discordant counts n = n10 + n01 and k = n10, the two-sided p-value is computed as p = 2 * min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 - BinomCDF(k - 1; n, 0.5)} with the conventional handling for k = 0. This exact-binom rule and the bootstrap parameters (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Task bank and deterministic selection. Tasks were generated deterministically using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and targeted high-difficulty workflow patterns (very_hard and extreme). The preregistration fixed a deterministic index-selection rule that produced the 200 tasks (adapter policy deterministic selection: cycle and offset pattern as recorded in the preregistration sampling_plan). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (ordered command list), allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., at-least-one-up constraints), difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count), and a normalized reference_answer. Representative archived manifests show required_command_count values ranging from 3 to 9 and changed_interface_count up to 3; these manifest fields are preserved in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and the representative_task entries in the bundle.

Model configuration and sampling semantics. The requested model declared in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini. That configuration records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; the hosted provider may sample nondeterministically. The adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Provider accounting in deterministic_reconciliation.json records stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 201. Cache metrics show cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0, indicating fresh generation events for all shared initial calls.

Deterministic verifier and scoring rule. The oracle was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. For each candidate, the verifier parses candidate configuration commands, maps them to task-encoded fields, checks that required_command_count is met, enforces ordering constraints (required_sequence), evaluates group and dependency invariants (minimum_active_in_groups, final_group_constraints, must_be_down_for_fields), and returns a binary full_intent_constraint_validation score (1 iff all invariants pass). Per-episode validator_trace artifacts include validation_before and validation_after states, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, and a boolean valid flag; these traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and provide the primary evidence for per-episode scoring decisions.

Paired execution semantics and failure handling. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics baseline and guarded episodes for each pair begin from the identical sampled candidate; any paired difference therefore arises solely from the permitted verifier-triggered repair. The preregistered missingness_plan included a deterministic syntax sanitizer for minor formatting fixes and a sensitivity analysis treating persistent unparsables as failures. In the archived run there were no persistent unparsables and no preregistered exclusions; all per-episode terminal_error_type fields are null in scoring artifacts. The primary analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) applied the exact McNemar test described above and computed paired-bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the absolute risk difference.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider-call audit. The execution manifest records start and end timestamps (UTC): started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00 (≈29 minutes wall-clock). Planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions) and completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}. These counts match the preregistered generation_semantics (one shared initial generation per task) plus the single permitted repair call exercised in one pair.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. analysis/condition_summary.csv shows baseline successes = 199, baseline failures = 1 (success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200, guarded failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Using the exact two-sided McNemar binomial calculation described in Methods (n = 1, k = 1) yields p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the absolute risk difference is [0.00, 0.015]; these values are identical to analysis/results.json and the archived CSVs.

Representative repaired case and diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair (stage_counts repair = 1). Validator traces indicate that the repaired pair involved an extreme composite task with required_command_count = 9 and changed_interface_count = 3 where the shared initial candidate violated the task's required_sequence ordering constraint. The repair applied a minimal reordering aligning the generated commands to the required_sequence; validation_after.valid = true in the post-repair trace. Representative artifact paths and validator_trace fields supporting this diagnostic include execution/scoring/task-000008-* and the per-episode validator_trace blocks archived in execution/scoring/; the task manifest for the repaired pair encodes the required_sequence and workflow_policies that defined the ordering constraint. This localized diagnostic supports the preregistered expectation that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity concentrate failure risk in higher-difficulty tasks.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination checks. The run recorded no preregistered exclusions and no persistent unparsables; analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 200 and zeros in all missingness categories. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (no flagged contamination). Deterministic_reconciliation.json indicates all deterministic consistency checks passed and pair_accounting_consistent = true. Provider-call cache fields (cache_miss_count = 201, cache_hit_count = 0) indicate fresh generation events. These artifact-grounded accounts show that the run executed as preregistered without exclusions or persistent failures.

Exploratory diagnostics by difficulty metadata. Representative task manifests in the archived sample illustrate variation in difficulty metadata (required_command_count from 3 to 9; patterns labeled very_hard or extreme). The single failed baseline episode occurred on an extreme composite task among the highest required_command_count values in the sample, consistent with the exploratory expectation that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity drive residual failure risk. analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg visualizes condition rates and the bootstrap distribution used for the CI calculation.

Compact numeric summaries. Table 1 and Table 2 (see captions) summarize the primary confirmatory numbers and provider-stage accounting. All numeric entries are drawn directly from the archived CSV artifacts and the execution manifest; analysis/*.csv and deterministic_reconciliation.json are the authoritative records.
sections.discussion:
Estimand interpretation and what the paired design measures. Because the experiment used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate the paired estimand isolates the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair on an identical sampled candidate: it is strictly a repair-only effect. This explicitly excludes any effect that would result from independent guarded first-pass re-generation, constrained-prompting variants, or larger multi-sample selection strategies; readers should not generalize the observed effect to those scenarios without new experiments.

Statistical regime, power, and inferential limits. The preregistered power rationale targeted detection of moderate absolute paired increases (~10–15 percentage points) at N = 200 assuming baseline pass rates near 45–65%. The observed baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) greatly exceeded these assumptions; this places the analysis in a discrete discordant-count regime where inference from McNemar's exact test is uninformative (p = 1.0 for the observed n = 1 discordant). The paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] provides a practical bound on plausible effect sizes compatible with the data and shows the data are consistent with at most small absolute improvements under our repair-only design.

Operational implications and bounded claims. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a narrow operational conclusion: in this synthetic task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a verifier-triggered bounded repair corrected a localized ordering fault on an identical initial candidate. We emphasize the limitation: this does not imply that guarded repair will systematically correct semantic intent misunderstandings, dataplane-only errors, or adversarially induced misconfigurations. Broader operational claims require (i) multi-model studies, (ii) experiments where guarded and baseline receive independent first-pass generations, (iii) live emulation or dataplane validation, and (iv) adversarial/contamination testing.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics ensure the estimand isolates repair effects and avoid confounding from independent sampling, but they do not address prompt sensitivity or sampling nondeterminism. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces invariants encoded in task manifests but cannot substitute for live dataplane execution—some runtime behaviors and device-specific interactions are unmodeled. External validity: the study used a single model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank; generalization to other models, vendor firmware, or production heterogeneity is not established. Conclusion validity: with only one discordant pair observed the sampling uncertainty for small absolute effects is substantial; the bootstrap CI quantifies this uncertainty.

Reproducibility and artifact guidance. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and indexed by the execution manifest. Key artifacts enabling reanalysis include: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (task selection and manifests), execution/model_configuration.json (declared model and sampling fields), execution/responses/ (shared-initial and per-condition responses), execution/scoring/ (validator_trace per episode), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv (confirmatory numbers), deterministic_reconciliation.json (provider accounting and stage_counts), and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (bootstrap parameters and seed). The exact initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 recorded in the Disclosure Statement). Reanalysis using the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor reproduces the confirmatory numbers reported above.

Practical diagnostic lessons from artifacts. The archived validator_traces are useful technical diagnostics: validation_before.violation_codes, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and normalized_configuration fields pinpoint where ordering or dependency checks failed. The single repair applied a minimal command reordering rather than wholesale semantic reinterpretation, suggesting that verifier-guided repairs that target sequence constraints can be effective for certain classes of errors in high-difficulty workflows. However, the artifacts also show that many tasks require multi-device coordination (changed_interface_count up to 3 and required_command_count up to 9), which increases the combinatorial space of valid command sequences and thus the potential for ordering-sensitive failures.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 synthetic deterministic tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair under the exact binomial formulation described in Methods. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived and indexed by the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
